questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to BENEVOLENT:
questions.e: Benevolent means well-meaning and generous. Related word: benefactor (one who helps others). Antonym: malevolent.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to CANDID:
questions.e: Candid means truthful and straightforward. The noun is candour.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to ABUNDANT:
questions.e: Abundant = existing in large quantities. Antonym: scarce or meagre.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to DILIGENT:
questions.e: Diligence is steady, earnest effort. Antonym: indolent.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to EMINENT:
questions.e: Eminent describes a famous and respected person. Do not confuse with imminent (about to happen) or immanent.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to VAGUE:
questions.e: Vague = not clearly expressed. Antonym: definite.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to MELANCHOLY:
questions.e: Melancholy is a pensive sadness. Related word: gloomy.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to PRAGMATIC:
questions.e: A pragmatic approach is based on practical results rather than theory.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to GENEROUS:
questions.e: Generous = ready to give. Stingy or miserly = unwilling to spend or give.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to ANCIENT:
questions.e: Ancient means very old; modern or contemporary is its antonym.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TRANSPARENT:
questions.e: Transparent allows light to pass through; opaque does not. Also used for honest and open governance.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to OPTIMISTIC:
questions.e: An optimist expects the best; a pessimist expects the worst.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to EXPAND:
questions.e: Expand = increase in size; contract = decrease.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to SCARCE:
questions.e: Scarce = in short supply. Plentiful and abundant are opposites.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to HUMBLE:
questions.e: Humble persons do not boast. Arrogant persons overrate themselves.

questions.q: The idiom 'to break the ice' means:
o: To start a conversation in an awkward situation
questions.e: It is used to ease tension when people meet for the first time.

questions.q: The idiom 'a piece of cake' means:
questions.e: The exam was a piece of cake means it was easy.

questions.q: The idiom 'once in a blue moon' means:
questions.e: It refers to a rare occurrence.

questions.q: The idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' means:
o: To work or study late into the night
questions.e: It comes from oil lamps used for night-time work.

questions.q: The idiom 'to cry over spilt milk' means:
o: To regret what cannot be undone
questions.e: It advises against grieving over past mistakes.

questions.q: The idiom 'to hit the nail on the head' means:
o: To say or do exactly the right thing
questions.e: It describes a precise, accurate remark.

questions.q: The idiom 'a blessing in disguise' means:
o: A good thing that seemed bad at first
A secret blessing from a saint
questions.e: It is used when a misfortune turns out beneficial.

questions.q: The idiom 'to beat around the bush' means:
questions.e: It means speaking indirectly without coming to the point.

questions.q: The idiom 'to bite the bullet' means:
o: To face a difficult situation bravely
questions.e: It comes from the practice of biting a bullet during surgery without anaesthesia.

questions.q: The phrase 'under the weather' means:
questions.e: It is a common idiom for mild illness.

questions.q: One who loves books is called a:
questions.e: Bibliophile = book lover; philatelist collects stamps; philanthropist loves mankind; misanthrope hates mankind.

questions.q: Fear of heights is called:
questions.e: Claustrophobia is fear of closed spaces; hydrophobia is fear of water; xenophobia is fear of foreigners.

questions.q: One who knows everything is:
questions.e: Omnipotent = all-powerful; omnipresent = present everywhere.

questions.q: The study of birds is called:
questions.e: Entomology is the study of insects; herpetology is the study of reptiles and amphibians.

questions.q: A medicine that cures all diseases is a:
questions.e: Panacea = universal remedy. Antidote counteracts poison.

questions.q: Something lasting for a very short time is:
questions.e: Ephemeral comes from Greek for 'lasting a day'.

questions.q: Murder of a king is called:
questions.e: Patricide is killing a father; fratricide killing a brother; infanticide killing an infant.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He ___ to school every day.
questions.e: The simple present uses the verb with 's' for the third person singular subject.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Neither of the boys ___ present.
questions.e: 'Neither' takes a singular verb. Similarly 'each' and 'either' are followed by singular verbs.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She has been living here ___ 2015.
questions.e: 'Since' is used for a point of time; 'for' is used for a duration (for ten years).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: I look forward to ___ you soon.
questions.e: 'To' in 'look forward to' is a preposition, so a gerund (-ing form) follows.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.e: Use 'an' before a vowel sound; 'honest' begins with a silent h, so a vowel sound.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: He is good ___ mathematics.
questions.e: Good at (a subject or skill); interested in; fond of; afraid of.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: She was accused ___ theft.
questions.e: Accused of; charged with; suspected of.

questions.q: Change into passive voice: 'The teacher praised the students.'
o: The students are praised by the teacher.
The students had praised the teacher.
The teacher was praised by students.
The students were praised by the teacher.
questions.e: Past simple active becomes 'was/were + past participle' in the passive.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: He said, 'I am happy.'
o: He said that I was happy.
He said that he is happy.
He told that he was happy.
He said that he was happy.
questions.e: In reported speech the present tense shifts to the past tense and the pronoun changes accordingly.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.e: Accommodation has double c and double m. Other tricky spellings: necessary, occurrence, separate, definitely.

questions.q: The plural of 'phenomenon' is:
questions.e: Other Latin/Greek plurals: criterion–criteria; datum–data; analysis–analyses; crisis–crises.

questions.q: The past participle of 'write' is:
questions.e: Write–wrote–written. Similarly: go–went–gone; see–saw–seen.

questions.q: In the sentence 'Honesty is the best policy', the word 'Honesty' is a/an:
questions.e: Abstract nouns name qualities or ideas that cannot be touched, such as love, courage and honesty.

questions.q: In the sentence 'She sings beautifully', the word 'beautifully' is a/an:
questions.e: Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or other adverbs and often end in -ly.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
o: Each of the students have completed the task.
Each of the students has completed the task.
Each of the students are completing the tasks.
Each of the student has completed the task.
questions.e: 'Each' is singular so it takes 'has'.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to RESILIENT:
questions.e: A resilient child bounces back from hardship. Resilience is a key concept in child protection and psychology.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BRIEF:
questions.e: Brief means short in duration or words; lengthy or prolonged is the opposite.

questions.q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to ENORMOUS:
questions.e: Enormous = very large.
